name: status-vocabulary
description: One status vocabulary, maintained by the loop

constraints.text: No schema enum changes: the vocabulary already in the schema is the truth; code constants are added to match it, not to redefine it.
Spine mode (sdd.json) keeps its own state set; it is legacy and out of scope.

scenarios.given: a pack authored without a status field
scenarios.then: the file carries status active explicitly
scenarios.when: the machine loads and saves it

scenarios.then: the file bytes are unchanged and the command reports COMPLETE

requirements.text: The machine MUST make pack status explicit: any machine-touched pack carries status active or complete, never an implicit absent; and a complete pack MUST never be rewritten by the loop, not even byte-identically.

scenarios.given: the schema, the code constants, and the wiki vocabulary page
scenarios.then: all three agree on every status family

requirements.text: The status vocabulary MUST have one source of truth: code constants for every stored and reported status family, a guard test that the vendored schema enums equal those constants, and a wiki page that documents the full table.
Complete packs MUST be positioned as read-only reference for future loops; the primer and the wiki MUST say so, and this pack MUST close itself to become the first reference under the new rule.

spec.why: A complete pack is reference material for future loops: queries, semantic search, cross-spec learning. That only works if statuses are one consistent, machine-maintained vocabulary. Today status is implicit when absent, the enums live only in the schema json, and a frozen pack is still re-saved byte-for-byte by next.

design.approach: Materialize explicit status at load (persisted by the next save), skip the save for COMPLETE handouts, add the vocabulary constants plus a schema-equality guard, document the table in the wiki, then close this pack as the first reference.

decisions.because: Complete packs become queryable reference material only if every consumer can trust the same closed sets; conventions drift, constants and guards do not.
decisions.decision: Statuses are one machine-maintained vocabulary: stored statuses (pack, task, decision, question, verdict) and reported statuses (handout results) are defined once, guarded against the schema, and documented on one wiki page.

decisions.because: Reference value depends on immutability; byte-identical re-saves are harmless today but break change detection and trust tomorrow.
decisions.decision: A complete pack is read-only reference: the loop reports from it (COMPLETE, check, status) but never rewrites it, not even byte-identically; new work opens a new pack that references the old one.

designs.detail: load_specpack materializes status active when absent (in memory; persisted by whichever save follows). The CLI never saves a COMPLETE handout: a frozen pack's bytes stay untouched. Comparisons use the PACK_STATUSES constants.
designs.title: Explicit status and the frozen non-touch

designs.detail: specpack.py defines PACK_STATUSES, TASK_STATUSES, DECISION_STATUSES, QUESTION_STATUSES, VERDICTS, and HANDOUT_STATUSES. A test parses the vendored schema and asserts every enum equals its constant. The wiki page domain/specpack-status-vocabulary.md documents the table: level, statuses, who sets them, stored or reported, terminality.
designs.title: Single-source vocabulary with a guard

notes: The frozen specpack-context pack is reference only; this wave must not touch its bytes.

read.why: the frozen reference pack this wave builds on
